title: MLS Hopes World Cup Fever Brings New Fans to Soccer in the U.S.
summary:
The World Cup is ending, but Major League Soccer (MLS) is just getting started. MLS wants to use the World Cup excitement to bring in new fans. They have a new ad campaign called "Thanks World, We'll Take It From Here" with soccer star Lionel Messi.

One example is the Chicago Fire. Chicago didn't host any World Cup games, so the team spent $3 million to build a huge watch party at a bar called Recess. Over 60,000 people came to watch games there! The Fire hopes these fans will come to their games too.

MLS also has a promotion called "First Match on Us" where 22 clubs give free tickets to people who have never been to a game. Brian Bilello from the New England Revolution says that in the 1990s, many sports fans thought soccer was boring. But now, more people are open to trying it.

Since Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023, more people have been watching MLS. The league hopes that this summer's World Cup will make soccer even more popular in the U.S.
why_it_matters: When something you love becomes popular, like a video game or a sport, more people want to join in—just like MLS is using the World Cup to help you discover a new team or make new friends who love soccer.

background_read: Major League Soccer (MLS) was founded in 1996 and has grown to 29 teams in the US and Canada. It has become a popular destination for famous international players.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, which has created a lot of excitement and opportunity for growing soccer in North America.
The Chicago Fire is an MLS team that plays in Illinois, and they hoped that by hosting a huge watch party for World Cup games, they could turn casual fans into loyal supporters.
Article_Structure: WHO: Major League Soccer (MLS) and its teams, with special mention of the Chicago Fire, Inter Miami, and the New England Revolution.
WHAT: They are launching an ad campaign with Lionel Messi, building watch parties, and giving free tickets to attract new fans to soccer.
WHERE: In the United States, with an example of a watch party at the Recess bar in Chicago.
WHY: To take advantage of the World Cup excitement and change the idea that soccer is boring, so more Americans will attend MLS games and follow the league.

perspectives.description: They are very hopeful that the World Cup will bring millions of new fans and more money to their clubs, making the league stronger.
They are glad to see the sport they love finally getting more attention in the US, after years of being considered less important than football or basketball.
They still think soccer is boring or too slow compared to other sports, and believe a short World Cup buzz won't change their minds in the long run.
